\title{Exact degree-ten invariants of a self-dual five-form\\ in ten dimensions}

\author{\pending{Author list pending mentor review}}

\abstract{%
A self-dual five-form in ten dimensions carries a $\dimSelfDualModule$-dimensional
space of field values, and the Lorentz-invariant scalar functions built from it
organise the possible non-linear self-interactions of the field. We determine
the degree-ten sector of this invariant structure exactly.

Working in two independent formulations --- a tensor formulation built from
contraction graphs, and a spinor formulation built from chiral bispinors --- we
construct an explicit map between them and certify that it is injective with
image the gamma-traceless subspace, of rank $\bridgeForwardRank$, with an exact
left inverse --- a left inverse, not a two-sided one, since the map is not onto
the full symmetric square. The two formulations are then compared degree by
degree on common samples, and their spans agree at degrees four, six, eight and
ten.

Three results are established exactly over the rationals rather than modulo a
prime. The full degree-ten invariant space has dimension $\dimAtenQ$. The
subspace reachable by the stress-tensor flow has dimension $\dimDtenQ$, computed
by running the closure to its fixed point in exact rational arithmetic after
lifting its non-integral targets by rational reconstruction. The quotient of the
first by the second therefore has dimension $\dimQtenQ$: there are three
independent degree-ten invariant directions that this flow does not reach. We
also show that the span of the previously published degree-ten structures meets
the product sector in exactly one dimension, and we write that intersection out
as an explicit integer identity.

For the generic functional rank of the full candidate family we certify the
lower bound $\charZeroLowerBound$ by an exact modular Jacobian computation with
an explicit $\minorSize\times\minorSize$ minor; the matching upper bound is
analytic and is due to earlier work, which we cite rather than reprove.

All results are supported by machine-checked certificates, and the computations
are reproducible from a public repository. We state explicitly which claims are
theorems, which are exact certificates, which rest on agreement across several
primes, and which remain open.%
}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

A chiral, or self-dual, $p$-form field is one whose field strength is
constrained to equal its own Hodge dual. The constraint is natural and it is
forced on us in several places in string theory, but it sits awkwardly with the
usual machinery of field theory: a self-dual field strength cannot be derived
from a manifestly Lorentz-invariant action in the naive way, a difficulty
identified by Marcus and Schwarz~\cite{Marcus:1982yu} and since addressed by a
sequence of increasingly satisfactory constructions --- the non-manifestly
covariant Hamiltonian formulation of Henneaux and
Teitelboim~\cite{Henneaux:1988gg}, the duality-symmetric actions of Schwarz and
Sen~\cite{Schwarz:1993vs}, the auxiliary-scalar formulation of Pasti,
Sorokin and Tonin~\cite{Pasti:1995tn,Pasti:1997gx}, the decoupled-auxiliary-field
action of Sen~\cite{Sen:2019qit}, and the covariant polynomial actions of
Mkrtchyan~\cite{Mkrtchyan:2019wnk}. The constraints on \emph{interacting} chiral
forms were sharpened early by Perry and Schwarz~\cite{Perry:1996mk}, whose
six-dimensional Born--Infeld analysis supplies the condition a self-interacting
chiral form must satisfy, and by Bekaert and Henneaux~\cite{Bekaert:1998yp}, who
derive that condition from the Dirac--Schwinger requirement on the
energy--momentum tensor and set out the topological subtleties in splitting a
non-chiral form into two chiral halves.

Once one asks not merely for \emph{a} self-dual theory but for the space of
\emph{non-linear} self-interactions a chiral form can have, the question becomes
one about scalar invariants. A Lagrangian, or in formulations where no Lagrangian
is available a deformation of the duality constraint, is built from
Lorentz-invariant scalar functions of the field strength. Knowing which such
functions exist, how many are independent, and how they are related is therefore
a prerequisite to classifying the theories. In four dimensions this is easy:
there are two invariants, the story is classical, and even the non-linear
duality-invariant theories that extend Maxwell's equations while preserving
conformal invariance have been completely
characterised~\cite{Bandos:2020hgy}, and subsequently extended to a
supersymmetric setting~\cite{Bandos:2021rqy}. In six dimensions the
analysis of self-interacting chiral two-forms is by now well
developed~\cite{Townsend:2019ftg,Ferko:2024chiral}, and the interplay with
$T\bar T$-like stress-tensor flows is understood in some
detail~\cite{Brizio:2026ttbar}.

The stress-tensor flow that supplies the deformation studied here has its own
lineage. The $T\bar T$ operator is well defined as a composite because its
expectation value factorises~\cite{Zamolodchikov:2004ce}; the flow it generates
was identified as a solvable direction in the space of two-dimensional theories
by Smirnov and Zamolodchikov~\cite{Smirnov:2016lqw} and, independently, by
Cavagli\`a, Negro, Sz\'ecs\'enyi and Tateo~\cite{Cavaglia:2016oda}, and it
admits a geometric reading as a field-dependent change of
coordinates~\cite{Conti:2018tca}. What we use at degree ten is the
higher-dimensional analogue of the flow, not these two-dimensional results
themselves; they are cited to fix what the construction is modelled on.

Ten dimensions is harder, and the difficulty is not conceptual but
combinatorial. The self-dual five-form lives in a $\dimSelfDualModule$-dimensional
module of $\mathrm{Spin}(1,9)$, the invariants of low degree are already
numerous, and the number of contraction patterns one can write down at degree ten
is large enough that hand enumeration is unreliable. Cederwall, Hutomo, Kuzenko,
Lechner and Sorokin~\cite{Cederwall:2025invariants} give explicit degree-ten
structures and analyse the invariant content of the five-form; the companion
paper of Hutomo, Lechner and Sorokin~\cite{Hutomo:2025chiral} develops the
non-linear chiral four-form theories in $D=10$ and the stress-tensor flow whose
reach is one of the objects we study here. What those works leave open, and what
this paper supplies, is the exact dimension of the degree-ten invariant space,
the exact dimension of the part of it the flow reaches, and the exact relation
between the published structures and the products of lower invariants.

\paragraph{Prior computational method.}
The general workflow we use --- enumerate contraction graphs, evaluate the
resulting invariants on generated tensor data, and read off the linear relations
from the ranks --- is not new, and we do not claim it. It is the method of
Elamaran, Ferko and Scarlett~\cite{Elamaran:2025mlinv}, who introduce it and
demonstrate it on a three-form in six dimensions. Our contribution on the
computational side is not the workflow but the certification: we replace
floating-point rank determination with exact arithmetic, and we attach to each
dimension a certificate that a reader can check independently.

\paragraph{Why exactness matters here.}
A rank computed in floating point is a judgement about how small a singular
value has to be before it counts as zero. For the questions in this paper that
judgement is exactly the thing at issue: the difference between
$\dim \Qten = \dimQtenQ$ and $\dim \Qten = 0$ is the difference between three
invariant directions the flow misses and none, and an earlier stage of this
project got that answer wrong for reasons that a tolerance would have concealed
rather than revealed (section~\ref{sec:reach}). Every rank quoted below is
therefore computed exactly, either in a finite field or over $\Q$.

\paragraph{Contributions.}
\begin{enumerate}\itemsep2pt
\item An explicit tensor--spinor bridge for the ten-dimensional self-dual
five-form, certified to have rank $\bridgeForwardRank$ onto the gamma-traceless
symmetric chiral bispinors, with an exact left inverse, a verified round trip and
verified equivariance (section~\ref{sec:bridge}).
\item A degree-resolved verification that the tensor and spinor formulations span
the same invariants at degrees four, six, eight and ten
(section~\ref{sec:equivalence}).
\item The exact rational dimensions
$\dim_\Q \Ften = \dimAtenQ$, $\dim_\Q \Dten = \dimDtenQ$ and
$\dim_\Q \Qten = \dimQtenQ$, with explicit minors and annihilating covectors
(section~\ref{sec:reach}).
\item An analytic derivation that the free stress-tensor trace vanishes at
quadratic order, together with a counterfactual showing the derivation is
load-bearing: assuming otherwise returns $\Qten = \gTenCounterfactualQten$
(section~\ref{sec:gten}).
\item The exact intersection $\dim_\Q(\Bten \cap \Pten) = \dimBcapP$, written out
as an integer identity (section~\ref{sec:published}).
\item An exact certification of the generic functional rank
$\charZeroLowerBound$ as a lower bound, over the complete
$\exactJacScheduled$-candidate family, with an explicit
$\minorSize\times\minorSize$ minor (section~\ref{sec:rank}).
\item A reproducibility architecture in which every number in this paper is
generated from a certificate rather than transcribed
(section~\ref{sec:repro}).
\end{enumerate}

% ================================================================ 2
\section{Ten-dimensional self-dual five-forms}
\label{sec:setup}

We work on $\mathbb{R}^{1,9}$ with metric $\eta = \mathrm{diag}(-1,+1,\dots,+1)$
and a fixed orientation, with volume form $\epsilon_{\mu_1\dots\mu_{10}}$
normalised by $\epsilon_{01\dots 9} = +1$. The Hodge star acts on a five-form by
\begin{equation}
(\star F)_{\mu_1\dots\mu_5}
 = \frac{1}{5!}\,\epsilon_{\mu_1\dots\mu_5}{}^{\nu_1\dots\nu_5}
   F_{\nu_1\dots\nu_5}.
\end{equation}
In Lorentzian signature and for a middle-degree form in ten dimensions
$\star^2 = +\starSquared$, so the star has real eigenvalues $\pm 1$ and the
space of five-forms splits,
\begin{equation}
\Lambda^5 = \Lambda^5_+ \oplus \Lambda^5_-,
\qquad
\dim \Lambda^5 = \dimFiveFormComponents,
\qquad
\dim \Lambda^5_\pm = \dimSelfDualModule .
\end{equation}
A self-dual five-form is an element of $\Lambda^5_+$, cut out by the projector
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
P_\pm \;=\; \tfrac12\bigl(\mathbf{1} \pm \star\bigr),
\qquad
P_\pm^{2} = P_\pm,
\\[2pt]
P_+ + P_- = \mathbf{1},
\qquad
\operatorname{tr} P_\pm = \dimSelfDualModule .
\end{gathered}
\label{eq:sdprojector}
\end{equation}
Throughout, $F$ denotes an element of $\Lambda^5_+$ and the whole discussion is
about polynomial functions of its $\dimSelfDualModule$ components.

That $\star^2 = +\starSquared$ rather than $-1$ is what makes
\eqref{eq:sdprojector} a real projector, and it is a coincidence of signature and
dimension rather than a general fact. For a $p$-form in $d$ dimensions with
$d = 2p$ and metric signature $(t,s)$,
\begin{equation}
\star^{2} \;=\; (-1)^{p(d-p)+t} \;=\; (-1)^{p^{2}+t}
\quad\text{(middle degree),}
\label{eq:starsquared}
\end{equation}
which for $p = 5$, $d = 10$ gives $\star^2 = -(-1)^{t}$: real eigenvalues
$\pm1$ in Lorentzian signature ($t = 1$), and eigenvalues $\pm i$ with no real
eigenspace decomposition in Euclidean signature ($t = 0$). Self-duality in ten
Lorentzian dimensions is thus available for a five-form and unavailable for its
Euclidean counterpart, and \eqref{eq:starsquared} is asserted by test wherever
the decomposition is used rather than assumed --- this project once mistook a
Euclidean projector for an anti-self-dual one and briefly read the resulting
non-vanishing as signal.

This is also the source of the difficulty that motivates the whole subject. The
self-duality constraint $\star F = F$ is a first-order condition on the field
strength, and imposing it on a $p$-form with $p$ odd obstructs the naive
construction of a manifestly Lorentz-invariant action, as Marcus and
Schwarz~\cite{Marcus:1982yu} observed: the kinetic term
$\langle F,F\rangle$ vanishes identically on the constrained surface, by exactly
the computation carried out in \eqref{eq:wedgevanishes} below. Every construction
cited in section~\ref{sec:intro} is a way around that vanishing.

The Lorentz group acts on $\Lambda^5_+$, and the objects of interest are the
polynomial functions invariant under that action. We grade them by degree in
$F$; because $F$ appears polynomially and the invariants are built by full
contraction, only even degrees occur, and we write $A_d$ for the space of
invariants of field degree $d$. This paper is about $A_{10}$, with $A_4$, $A_6$
and $A_8$ appearing as inputs and as consistency checks.

\paragraph{Generic orbit dimension.}
The Lorentz algebra has dimension $\dimLorentzAlgebra$. A generic point of
$\Lambda^5_+$ has a stabiliser, and the dimension of the generic orbit is
$\dimLorentzAlgebra$ minus the dimension of that stabiliser. The count of
functionally independent invariants at a generic point is correspondingly
$\dimSelfDualModule$ minus the generic orbit dimension. This analytic count is
$\genericFunctionalDim$ and it is not ours; it appears in the literature we build
on~\cite{Hutomo:2025chiral}. What we contribute is an exact computational lower
bound matching it, discussed in section~\ref{sec:rank}.

\paragraph{Real and complex statements.}
It matters, and it will matter again in section~\ref{sec:bridge}, whether a given
statement is about a real form or about the complexification. Dimension counts of
invariant spaces are statements about the complexified problem and are insensitive
to the real form. Statements about which eigenspace of $\star$ is which, by
contrast, are not: they depend on signature and orientation, and getting them
wrong is a silent error rather than a loud one.

% ================================================================ 3
\section{Tensor formulation}
\label{sec:tensor}

In the tensor formulation an invariant is specified by a contraction pattern.
Write $F$ with its five indices, take some number of copies, and contract all
indices in pairs using $\eta$. Each such pattern is naturally encoded as a graph:
vertices are copies of $F$, and edges are index contractions, with each vertex
carrying five ports.

Two different-looking contraction patterns can define the same invariant, so the
graphs must be reduced to a canonical form before they are counted. We do this
with the \texttt{nauty} canonical labelling of McKay and
Piperno~\cite{McKay:2013}, reached through the \texttt{pynauty} bindings. This
step is not a convenience: an earlier version of this project used an inexact
hashing fallback which collided, mapping distinct classes onto the same key and
undercounting the atlas. Canonicalisation here is exact at every degree used.

Two structured tensors recur and are worth naming. From two copies of $F$ one
builds the symmetric tensor
\begin{equation}
M_{\mu\nu} = F_{\mu\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}\,
             F_\nu{}^{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta},
\end{equation}
whose traces $\operatorname{Tr}(M^k)$ furnish a convenient family of invariants,
and from four copies one builds the two irreducible structures we label
$N^{(1050)}$ and $N^{(4125)}$ after the dimensions of the $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$
representations in which they transform. Index placement conventions for all
three are fixed in appendix~\ref{app:blocks}; they are stated there rather than
here because nothing in the argument depends on the choice, only on its
consistency.

We distinguish throughout between \emph{product} invariants --- those that
factorise as a product of invariants of strictly lower degree, such as
$I^{(4)}_1 I^{(6)}_1$ at degree ten --- and \emph{primitive} invariants, which do
not. The product subspace at degree ten is written $\Pten$; the span of the
graph generators is written $\Gten$. Table~\ref{tab:notation} collects the
notation.

\input{tables/tab01_notation.tex}

% ================================================================ 4
\section{Spinor formulation}
\label{sec:spinor}

The second formulation replaces the five-form by a bispinor. In ten dimensions
the chiral spinor module $S_+$ has dimension $\spinorDim$. The symmetric square
$\mathrm{Sym}^2 S_+$ has dimension $\dimSymSpinor$, and it carries a gamma-trace
map whose image accounts for $\gammaTraceRank$ of those dimensions. The kernel of
the gamma trace therefore has dimension
$\dimSymSpinor - \gammaTraceRank = \dimGammaTraceless$, matching
$\dim \Lambda^5_+$ exactly. This coincidence of dimensions is the reason a bridge
between the two formulations can exist at all; the Clifford-algebra facts behind
it, including the existence of Majorana--Weyl spinors in this signature, are
standard and we follow the conventions of Kugo and
Townsend~\cite{Kugo:1982bn}.

Invariants in this formulation are built by contracting copies of the bispinor
with gamma matrices and charge-conjugation matrices along closed index paths. We
organise these as \emph{port graphs}, the spinor-side analogue of the tensor
contraction graphs. In addition to the port graphs we admit a family of
\emph{tensor words}: expressions in which a tensor-side structure is used as an
intermediate. Whether the tensor words are needed is not an aesthetic question,
and section~\ref{sec:equivalence} shows that at degree eight they are: removing
them lowers the rank. The candidates denoted $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the
detailed inventory of appendix~\ref{app:bases} belong to this family.

Full conventions --- chirality, charge conjugation, the symmetry properties of
$C\Gamma^{(k)}$ and the normalisation of the five-gamma --- are in
appendix~\ref{app:conventions}.

% ================================================================ 5
\section{Real forms and the exact tensor--spinor bridge}
\label{sec:bridge}

\subsection{The map}

The bridge sends a self-dual five-form to a symmetric chiral bispinor by
contracting with the five-index gamma:
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
\Phi: \Lambda^5_+ \longrightarrow \mathrm{Sym}^2 S_+, \\[2pt]
\Phi(F)_{ab} = \frac{1}{5!}\,F_{\mu_1\dots\mu_5}\,
              (C\Gamma^{\mu_1\dots\mu_5})_{ab}.
\end{gathered}
\label{eq:bridge}
\end{equation}
That $C\Gamma^{(5)}$ is symmetric in $ab$, so that the image lies in the
symmetric square, is a property of the ten-dimensional Clifford algebra; it is
verified directly in the implementation rather than assumed.

The target of \eqref{eq:bridge} is not all of $\mathrm{Sym}^2 S_+$. Writing the
gamma trace as the contraction
\begin{equation}
(\gamma\text{-}\mathrm{tr}\,\psi)_\mu
 \;=\; \eta_{\mu\nu}\,(\Gamma^{\nu})^{ab}\,\psi_{ab},
\qquad
\psi \in \mathrm{Sym}^2 S_+,
\label{eq:gammatrace}
\end{equation}
a dimension count fixes the image exactly. With $\dim S_+ = \spinorDim$ we have
$\dim \mathrm{Sym}^2 S_+ = \tfrac12\spinorDim(\spinorDim+1) = \dimSymSpinor$,
while \eqref{eq:gammatrace} has rank $\gammaTraceRank$, one for each value of
$\mu$. Hence
\begin{equation}
\dim\ker(\gamma\text{-}\mathrm{tr})
 \;=\; \dimSymSpinor - \gammaTraceRank
 \;=\; \dimGammaTraceless
 \;=\; \dim\Lambda^5_+ ,
\vphantom{\bigl|}
\label{eq:dimcount}
\end{equation}
and the two spaces have equal dimension. Equality of dimensions is of course not
equality of spaces, and the substance of the following proposition is that the
map realises the isomorphism the count permits.

\begin{proposition}[Certified properties of the bridge]
\label{prop:bridge}
Over $\Fp$, for each prime used, the map \eqref{eq:bridge} satisfies
\begin{align}
\mathrm{im}\,\Phi &\;=\; \ker(\gamma\text{-}\mathrm{tr}),
  &\mathrm{rank}\,\Phi &\;=\; \bridgeForwardRank,
  \label{eq:bridgerank}\\
\ker\Phi \cap \Lambda^5_+ &\;=\; 0,
  &\Phi\big|_{\Lambda^5_-} &\;\equiv\; 0,
  \label{eq:bridgekernel}\\
\Phi^-\Phi &\;=\; \mathrm{id}_{\dimSelfDualModule},
  &\Phi\,\Phi^- &\;=\; \Pi_{\gamma\text{-}\mathrm{tr}},
  \label{eq:bridgeinverse}
\end{align}
where $\Pi_{\gamma\text{-}\mathrm{tr}}$ is the projector onto
$\ker(\gamma\text{-}\mathrm{tr})$, and, for $\Lambda$ in the Lorentz group with
spinor representative $S(\Lambda)$,
\begin{equation}
\Phi(\Lambda\cdot F)
 \;=\; \chi(\Lambda)\; S(\Lambda)\,\Phi(F)\,S(\Lambda)^{T},
\qquad
\chi \equiv 1 .
\label{eq:equivariance}
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

Three of these deserve comment, since each is a place where a weaker statement
would have been easy to mistake for the real one.

The second identity in \eqref{eq:bridgeinverse} is not a typographical variant of
the first. $\Phi$ has full column rank but is not surjective onto
$\mathrm{Sym}^2 S_+$, so it admits a left inverse and no two-sided one;
$\Phi\Phi^-$ is a projector of rank $\bridgeForwardRank$, not the identity on the
$\dimSymSpinor$-dimensional space. Both halves are checked as matrix identities
rather than on sampled vectors, because an identity that holds on a handful of
random $F$ and fails on a subspace is exactly the failure sampling cannot see.

The second identity in \eqref{eq:bridgekernel} is the sharp one. On the opposite
eigenspace the map does not merely lose rank, it vanishes identically. This is
forced by the chirality structure: on $S_+$ the anti-self-dual part of
$\Gamma^{(5)}$ annihilates the module and only the self-dual part acts, so
$\Phi$ is blind to $\Lambda^5_-$ by construction. That blindness is precisely
what makes an orientation error silent, and is the subject of
section~\ref{sec:orientation}.

In \eqref{eq:equivariance} the character $\chi$ is \emph{solved for} rather than
assumed. Asserting $\chi = 1$ and checking the resulting identity would test
nothing, since any discrepancy could be absorbed into an unverified constant;
solving for $\chi$ and finding it identically unity is a check that can fail.
Each statement in the proposition is verified by an explicit test at every prime
used, with no floating-point tolerance anywhere; the inventory is in
appendix~\ref{app:bridge-exact}. What we claim is the certification, not the
formula: \eqref{eq:bridge} is standard.

\subsection{Which real form, and why it is not a frame choice}

The spinor-side computation is naturally carried out in a null, or oscillator,
frame, which is adapted to split signature $(5,5)$. The physical problem is
Lorentzian, signature $(1,9)$. These two real forms share a complexification,
$\mathfrak{so}(10,\mathbb{C})$, and every dimension count in this paper is a
statement about that complexification, so no result depends on which real form
the arithmetic is done in. Precisely,
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak{so}(1,9)\otimes\mathbb{C}
 \;\cong\; \mathfrak{so}(10,\mathbb{C})
 \;\cong\; \mathfrak{so}(5,5)\otimes\mathbb{C},
\label{eq:realforms}
\end{equation}
and every dimension, rank and intersection reported below is the dimension of a
$\mathbb{C}$-linear object, hence constant along \eqref{eq:realforms}.

We state one thing explicitly because an earlier version of this project recorded
the opposite and it took some effort to correct: the Lorentzian and split real
forms are \emph{not} related by a real orthogonal frame transformation. There is
no $\Lambda \in O(1,9;\mathbb{R})$ carrying $\eta_{(1,9)}$ to $\eta_{(5,5)}$,
since a real congruence preserves the signature; the two are different real forms
of the same complex algebra, and only after complexifying are they identified.
What \eqref{eq:realforms} transports is dimension counts. What it does not
transport is the question of \emph{which} eigenspace of $\star$ survives, because
$\star$ is defined with $\eta$ and the reality of its eigenspaces is exactly a
signature-dependent statement --- the subject of the next subsection.

\subsection{The orientation branch, and a prime that exposed it}
\label{sec:orientation}

Implementing the null frame over $\Fp$ requires solving a congruence for the
frame matrix $L$, and that solution involves a square root. A square root over
$\Fp$ has two branches. The two branches differ by an orientation reversal, an
orientation reversal flips the sign of the Hodge star, and flipping the sign of
the star exchanges $\Lambda^5_+$ with $\Lambda^5_-$. The consequence is that with
the branch left unpinned, the construction computes the self-dual projector at
some primes and the \emph{anti}-self-dual projector at others, with nothing to
announce the difference.

This is not hypothetical. Three cells of the rank matrix of
section~\ref{sec:rank} failed at $p = 32707$, at every seed. The natural first
hypothesis --- an exceptional prime, to be excluded --- is wrong, and it is worth
recording how we know. Flipping the branch by hand at $p = 32707$ restores the
expected behaviour, and flipping it at a prime that had been working breaks that
prime in exactly the same way. The failure tracks the branch, not the prime.

The resolution was to pin the branch by construction rather than to exclude the
prime. The frame routine now selects, deterministically, the branch under which
the self-dual space is the surviving one, and raises an error if neither branch
works rather than guessing.

The mechanism is worth writing down, because the failure is silent. The null
frame is a matrix $L$ over $\Fp$ solving the congruence
\begin{equation}
L^{T}\,\eta\,L \;=\; \eta_{\mathrm{null}},
\label{eq:congruencebody}
\end{equation}
and \eqref{eq:congruencebody} determines $L$ only up to the square-root branches
taken while solving it. Two solutions $L$ and $L'$ of \eqref{eq:congruencebody}
with $\det L' = -\det L$ are both legitimate frames, but they induce
$\star \mapsto +\star$ and $\star \mapsto -\star$ respectively, and therefore
\begin{equation}
\Phi\big|_{\Lambda^5_+} \;\text{has rank } \bridgeForwardRank
\quad\text{versus}\quad
\Phi\big|_{\Lambda^5_+} \;\equiv\; 0,
\label{eq:branchconsequence}
\end{equation}
by \eqref{eq:bridgekernel}. Nothing in the arithmetic distinguishes them: the
wrong branch raises no error and returns a perfectly well-formed matrix of the
wrong eigenspace.

One caution about what this selection does and does not verify. The criterion
used to \emph{choose} the branch is that the composite have rank
$\dimSelfDualModule$, so reporting that rank afterwards would be circular as a
check even though the construction is sound. The independent check is a different
one: on the image of the selected construction we verify directly that
$\star F = +F$, that is, that the surviving eigenvalue is $+1$ and not $-1$. That
is a property of the output, not the criterion that produced it, and it is what
ties the implementation to the orientation convention fixed in
appendix~\ref{app:conventions}.

\begin{remark}
No number in this paper changed as a result of this fix. Every certificate had
been computed at a prime where the unpinned code happened to select correctly,
and recomputation after the fix returned identical values. What changed is that
the stated convention is now true by construction rather than true at the primes
that happened to be used. We report it because a convention that holds by
accident is a defect even when it has not yet produced a wrong number.
\end{remark}

% ================================================================ 6
\section{Exact computational methodology}
\label{sec:method}

\paragraph{Two independent evaluators.}
The tensor and spinor sides are implemented separately, with no shared
evaluation code. This is what makes the agreement of section~\ref{sec:equivalence}
informative: had one evaluator been a wrapper around the other, agreement would
have been a tautology.

\paragraph{Exact modular evaluation.}
Invariants are evaluated at sample points with coordinates in $\Fp$ for primes
near $2^{15}$, with reduction after every contraction step so intermediate values
cannot overflow. Ranks are obtained by exact Gaussian elimination over $\Fp$.
Contraction order is chosen by a greedy planner supplied by
\texttt{opt\_einsum}~\cite{Smith:2018}, which is a requirement rather than an
optional accelerator: it also supplies the intermediate-size and
floating-point-operation estimates that the contractor enforces as a hard
budget, so without it that budget is not checked at all
(appendix~\ref{app:reproduction}). Array handling throughout is
NumPy~\cite{Harris:2020}.

\paragraph{What a modular rank does and does not establish.}
A rank computed mod $p$ is a lower bound on the rank over $\Q$, and equals it
unless $p$ divides a relevant minor. Agreement across several primes makes an
unlucky coincidence implausible but does not prove anything. Two arguments close
this gap in the cases that matter.

First, the spanning-set argument. If a space is spanned by exactly $k$ explicit
elements then $\dim_\Q \le k$ for free, so a modular rank of $k$ pins the
rational dimension with no prime excluded. Applying this requires the spanning
elements to be defined over $\Q$, and it is worth being explicit that they are.
An invariant here is specified by a contraction graph --- an integer incidence
pattern --- and evaluating it contracts copies of $F$ with $\eta$ and $\epsilon$,
both of which have integer entries. Each candidate is therefore a polynomial with
\emph{integer} coefficients in the $\dimSelfDualModule$ coordinates, defined
before any prime is chosen; the prime enters only when that fixed polynomial is
evaluated. So $\Ften$, $\Gten$ and $\Pten$ are each spanned by an explicit
integer-coefficient family, and the argument applies to them. For $\Bten$ the
published structures are lifted to $\Q$ outright (appendix~\ref{app:b10}), so it
is covered twice over.

Second, where no spanning-set argument is available --- for
$\Dten$, and through it $\Qten$, since the closure produces its elements rather
than being handed them --- we lift to $\Q$ explicitly, by the
Chinese remainder theorem and rational reconstruction in the sense of Wang, Guy
and Davenport~\cite{Wang:1982}, and validate the lift at a prime held out of the
fit. Sampling arguments elsewhere in the pipeline are of Schwartz--Zippel
type~\cite{Zippel:1979,Schwartz:1980}.

\paragraph{Analytic derivatives.}
The Jacobian of section~\ref{sec:rank} is computed by analytic differentiation of
each invariant with respect to the $\dimSelfDualModule$ coordinates --- by
amputation of one $F$ from the contraction pattern --- and not by finite
differences. Every row is checked against Euler's homogeneity relation, which
gives an independent handle on differentiation errors: a row that fails Euler is
wrong regardless of what rank it would have contributed.

\paragraph{Determinants.}
Where a determinant certifies a rank we compute it twice, by fraction-free
Bareiss elimination~\cite{Bareiss:1968} and by an independent exact routine, and
require agreement.

\paragraph{Frozen executions and immutable artifacts.}
Each rank-matrix cell writes an immutable JSON artifact. Aggregation is a
separate, read-only, order-independent step. This separation exists because an
earlier incident in this project involved two processes sharing a row cache; the
architecture now makes that impossible rather than merely discouraged.

\paragraph{What is prior work.}
The enumerate--evaluate--relate workflow is due to Elamaran, Ferko and
Scarlett~\cite{Elamaran:2025mlinv}. Canonicalisation is
\texttt{nauty}~\cite{McKay:2013}. Bareiss elimination, CRT and rational
reconstruction are classical. What is new here is the certification layer: the
exact arithmetic throughout, the explicit minors, the held-out-prime validation,
the counterfactual tests, and the discipline that no number reaches the
manuscript except through a generated macro.

% ================================================================ 7
\section{Degree-resolved tensor--spinor equivalence}
\label{sec:equivalence}

The two formulations are compared on $\nCommonSamples$ common sample points at
prime $\comparisonPrime$, drawn from four families: sparse, structured, generic
and a held-out set used only for validation. For each degree we compute the rank
of the tensor family, the rank of the spinor family, and the rank of their union.
Equality of the first and third means the spinor family adds nothing the tensor
family did not already have, and vice versa.

The three ranks are listed degree by degree in table~\ref{tab:degranks} and
plotted in figure~\ref{fig:degranks}.

\input{tables/tab02_degree_ranks.tex}

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.72\textwidth]{figures/fig01_degree_spectrum.pdf}
\caption{Degree-resolved tensor, spinor and union ranks. At every degree shown
the three agree, so neither formulation sees an invariant the other misses.}
\label{fig:degranks}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Degrees four and six}
At degree four the invariant space is one-dimensional and at degree six it is
two-dimensional, in both formulations, with the spans equal and the equality
confirmed on held-out samples. These degrees are not in doubt and we record them
mainly as a check on the machinery.

\subsection{Degree eight, and an ablation}
\label{sec:deg8}
Degree eight is where the interesting structure appears. With the full spinor
candidate family,
\begin{equation}
\dim A_8^{\mathrm{tensor}} = \dim A_8^{\mathrm{spinor}}
 = \dim\bigl(A_8^{\mathrm{tensor}} + A_8^{\mathrm{spinor}}\bigr)
 = \dEightUnionRank ,
\end{equation}
at all $\dEightPrimesEqual$ of the $\dEightPrimes$ primes tested.

The full spinor family includes the tensor words of section~\ref{sec:spinor}.
Removing them drops the spinor-side rank from $\dEightSpinorRank$ to
$\dEightRankWithoutWords$, so one invariant direction is lost. The tensor words
are therefore not redundant. Figure~\ref{fig:ablation} shows the ablation, and
the candidate families it is run over are inventoried in
table~\ref{tab:candidates}.

\input{tables/tab05_candidates.tex}

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.62\textwidth]{figures/fig02_degree8_ablation.pdf}
\caption{Degree-eight family ablation. Removing the tensor words from the spinor
candidate family lowers the rank by one, so within this decomposition they are
indispensable.}
\label{fig:ablation}
\end{figure}

We state the conclusion in the qualified form the evidence supports: \emph{tensor
words are indispensable within the tested candidate-family decomposition}. This
is a statement about the families we constructed. It is not a uniqueness theorem,
and we do not claim that no other decomposition could reach rank
$\dEightUnionRank$ without them.

\begin{remark}[Two different degree-eight spinor ranks]
The reader comparing against intermediate artifacts of this project will find a
degree-eight spinor rank of $\dEightRankWithoutWords$ recorded alongside the
$\dEightSpinorRank$ quoted here. These are not in conflict: they are the ranks of
two different candidate families, before and after the tensor words are included.
The ablation above is exactly the difference between them.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Degree ten}
At degree ten both formulations give rank $\traceRankDegTen$, with equal spans
and held-out validation passing. This is the atlas dimension $\dim \Ften$ that
the rest of the paper uses.

We should be precise about what identifies this atlas dimension with the full
invariant space. The equality $\dim \Ften = \traceRankDegTen$ is exact for the
span of the candidates we enumerate; reading it as the dimension of \emph{all}
degree-ten Lorentz invariants additionally requires that the enumeration miss
nothing. Two independent constructions --- contraction graphs and chiral
bispinors --- were carried out separately and agree here and at degrees four,
six and eight, which is meaningful corroboration precisely because a shared
omission would have to occur twice in two different languages. It is not a
proof of exhaustiveness, and we do not present it as one; the point is recorded
again in section~\ref{sec:limitations}.

% ================================================================ 8
\section{Generic functional rank}
\label{sec:rank}

\subsection{The computation}
Let $I_1,\dots,I_N$ be the candidate invariants, $N = \exactJacScheduled$, each a
polynomial in the $n = \dimSelfDualModule$ coordinates $F^A$ of $\Lambda^5_+$.
The generic functional rank of the family is the rank at a generic point of the
Jacobian
\begin{equation}
J(F)^{\;A}_{i} \;=\; \frac{\partial I_i}{\partial F^A},
\qquad
i = 1,\dots,N,\quad A = 1,\dots,n,
\label{eq:jacobian}
\end{equation}
an $\exactJacRows \times \exactJacCols$ matrix. Each row is computed
\emph{analytically}, by amputating one factor of $F$ from the contraction
pattern that defines $I_i$, rather than by finite differences; there is no step
size and no cancellation error.

Each row carries an independent check. Since $I_i$ is homogeneous of field
degree $d_i$, Euler's relation gives
\begin{equation}
\sum_{A=1}^{n} F^{A}\,\frac{\partial I_i}{\partial F^{A}}
 \;=\; d_i\, I_i ,
\label{eq:euler}
\end{equation}
which relates a differentiated row to an undifferentiated evaluation and is
therefore sensitive to exactly the errors that differentiation introduces. A row
failing \eqref{eq:euler} is wrong whatever rank it would have contributed. Every
scheduled candidate was evaluated --- $\exactJacEvaluated$ of
$\exactJacScheduled$, with $\exactJacErrors$ errors and $\exactJacZeroRows$
identically-zero rows --- and \eqref{eq:euler} holds on every row.

The exact modular rank is $\exactJacRank$. Cumulative ranks by degree are
$\cumRankDegFour$, $\cumRankDegSix$, $\cumRankDegEight$, $\cumRankDegTen$ and
$\cumRankDegTwelve$ at degrees four, six, eight, ten and twelve respectively.
These increments are plotted in figure~\ref{fig:degranks}(b). No step in the
chain uses floating point and no step uses a tolerance: the candidates are
integer-coefficient polynomials, the Jacobian is differentiated analytically by
amputation, and the rank is obtained by exact elimination over $\Fp$.

\subsection{The certificate}
A rank claim backed only by an elimination is a claim about a program. We
therefore exhibit an explicit $\minorSize \times \minorSize$ minor whose
determinant is non-zero, computed by two independent routines that agree. Since a
non-vanishing minor over $\Fp$ lifts to a non-vanishing minor over $\Q$ --- the
determinant is an integer that is non-zero mod $p$ --- this gives the
characteristic-zero lower bound
\begin{equation}
\text{generic functional rank} \;\ge\; \charZeroLowerBound
\end{equation}
with no prime excluded and no appeal to genericity of the sample.

A rank is a number, and on its own it says nothing about \emph{which} invariants
realise it. Since the certificate names its own rows, that question can be
answered directly: figure~\ref{fig:pivots} sorts the $\minorSize$ pivot rows by
the degree of the candidate and by the family it was constructed in. Two
features matter for what follows. The pivots are spread across every degree
rather than concentrated at one, so the bound is not an artefact of the
degree-twelve block alone; and the tensor words supply pivots of their own,
which is the same conclusion the degree-eight ablation of
section~\ref{sec:deg8} reaches by a different route.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.95\textwidth]{figures/fig04_pivot_composition.pdf}
\caption{The $\minorSize$ pivot rows of the certified minor, read from the
certificate's own row list. Left, by the field degree of the candidate; right,
by the family it belongs to. Neither split is uniform, and neither is
concentrated in a single bucket.}
\label{fig:pivots}
\end{figure}

\subsection{The prime/sample matrix}
The computation was repeated across $\matrixPrimes$ primes and $\matrixSeeds$
seeds, giving $\matrixCells$ cells, set out in table~\ref{tab:matrix} and
figure~\ref{fig:matrix}. Every cell returns rank $\matrixRank$, and every cell
returns the \emph{same} $\matrixStableRows$ pivot rows and
$\matrixStableCols$ pivot columns, with $\matrixUnstableRows$ unstable.

We are deliberately restrained about what this establishes. Thirteen of the
$\matrixCells$ cells were produced by a single run in a separate working tree and
were not independently recomputed here, and cells from one run agreeing with each
other is close to guaranteed whether or not the run was correct. The agreement
across primes and seeds is therefore corroboration, not independent
confirmation. What carries weight is narrower and does not depend on the other
thirteen: the two cells recomputed in this repository agree with the certificate
on total rank, per-degree block ranks, cumulative ranks, pivot rows, pivot
columns and pivot row candidate identities; and the lower bound itself rests on a
single explicit minor (section~\ref{sec:rank}) that can be checked without
reference to the matrix at all.

\input{tables/tab06_matrix.tex}

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.66\textwidth]{figures/fig03_rank_matrix.pdf}
\caption{The prime/sample rank matrix. Every cell agrees on rank and on pivot
structure.}
\label{fig:matrix}
\end{figure}

\subsection{What is and is not claimed}
The upper bound is analytic and belongs to earlier
work~\cite{Hutomo:2025chiral}; combined with our lower bound it gives
$\genericFunctionalDim$ exactly. We claim the lower bound and the certificate,
not the number.

Two further cautions. First, the statement is about \emph{functional} rank at a
generic point: the selected family has generic functional rank
$\genericFunctionalDim$. We do \emph{not} claim that all $\exactJacScheduled$
candidates are algebraically independent, which is a different and stronger
assertion. Second, of the $\matrixCells$ cells, two were recomputed
independently in this repository and agree with the certificate on every recorded
quantity; the remaining thirteen were not independently recomputed here, and for
them what is established is internal consistency together with a shared
candidate-ordering hash. This is stated again in the limitations.

% ================================================================ 9
\section{Reachability of the stress flow at degree ten}
\label{sec:reach}

\subsection{Three spaces, two of which are easily confused}
The stress-tensor flow generates new invariants from old by repeatedly applying
a construction built from the stress tensor $\tau$ of the deformed
theory~\cite{Hutomo:2025chiral,Ferko:2024chiral}. Schematically, a deformation
parameter $\lambda$ drives
\begin{equation}
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial \lambda}
 \;=\; \mathcal{O}\bigl[\tau(\mathcal{L})\bigr],
\label{eq:flow}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal{O}$ is a scalar built from traces of powers of $\tau$. We do not
reproduce the construction of \cite{Hutomo:2025chiral} here; what the argument
below needs from it is only which trace monomials it produces and the field
degree at which each begins. Both were determined by instrumenting the closure
rather than by reading the construction, so that a generator consumed but not
documented would show up. Through degree ten the generators are exactly
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
&\operatorname{Tr}\tau, &&
\operatorname{Tr}\tau^{2}, &&
\operatorname{Tr}\tau^{3}, &&
\operatorname{Tr}\tau^{4}, &&
\operatorname{Tr}\tau^{5}, \\
&(\operatorname{Tr}\tau)^{2}, &&
\operatorname{Tr}\tau\operatorname{Tr}\tau^{2}, &&
\operatorname{Tr}\tau\operatorname{Tr}\tau^{3}, &&
(\operatorname{Tr}\tau^{2})^{2}, &&
\operatorname{Tr}\tau^{2}\operatorname{Tr}\tau^{3}.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:generators}
\end{equation}

Write $\deg_F$ for the leading field degree of an expression, that is, the lowest
power of $F$ appearing in it. The grading that controls the whole calculation is
\begin{equation}
\deg_F\!\left(\operatorname{Tr}\tau^{k}\right)
 \;=\;
 \begin{cases}
   4, & k = 1,\\[2pt]
   2k, & k \ge 2,
 \end{cases}
\qquad
\deg_F\!\left(\prod_i \operatorname{Tr}\tau^{k_i}\right)
 \;=\; \sum_i \deg_F\!\left(\operatorname{Tr}\tau^{k_i}\right).
\label{eq:leadingdegree}
\end{equation}
The exceptional case $k = 1$ is the content of theorem~\ref{thm:gten}: the naive
count would give $\deg_F\operatorname{Tr}\tau = 2$, and it is the vanishing of
the free trace that pushes it to $4$. Every entry of \eqref{eq:leadingdegree}
was checked independently at every prime, with no exceptions.

A target is \emph{generated} when the flow produces it formally, and
\emph{activated} at degree $d$ when \eqref{eq:leadingdegree} permits it to
contribute there. Writing $V_d$ for the span reached at degree $d$, the closure
is the least fixed point of
\begin{equation}
V \;\longmapsto\;
 V + \mathrm{span}\bigl\{\,g \;:\; g \text{ generated from } V,\;
 \deg_F g \le d \,\bigr\},
\label{eq:closureoperator}
\end{equation}
started from the degree-four seed and iterated until a sweep raises no rank.
Termination occurred after $\czSweeps$ sweeps, and over $\Q$ the reachable
dimensions by degree are $1$, $2$, $7$ and $\dimDtenQ$ at degrees four, six,
eight and ten.

Two structural facts make the question below well posed. The map induced by
\eqref{eq:flow} on each graded piece is linear, and $\Dten$ is by construction
the \emph{span} of the reachable elements; so $\Dten$ is a linear subspace of
$\Ften$ and the quotient $\Qten = \Ften/\Dten$ is defined. Asking what the flow
reaches at degree ten then requires three spaces to be kept apart.

\begin{definition}\leavevmode
\begin{itemize}\itemsep2pt
\item The \emph{full invariant space} $\Ften$: all degree-ten Lorentz invariants.
\item The \emph{raw target span}: the span of every target the flow generates,
      \emph{ignoring} whether the flow can actually activate it at this degree.
\item The \emph{activated closure} $\Dten$: the span of what the flow actually
      reaches, obtained by iterating activation to a fixed point.
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}

The raw target span has dimension $\dimAten$ --- the same as $\dim \Ften$. If one
identifies it with $\Dten$, the quotient comes out zero and the conclusion is
that the flow reaches everything. That identification is false, and this project
made it before catching it. In symbols, writing $\mathcal{T}$ for the set of targets the flow generates and
$\mathcal{A}$ for the activation rule of section~\ref{sec:gten},
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{span}\,\mathcal{T} \;=\; \Ften
\qquad\text{but}\qquad
\Dten \;=\; \mathrm{span}\!\left(\bigcup_{k\ge 0}\mathcal{A}^{k}(\mathcal{T}_0)\right)
 \;\subsetneq\; \Ften,
\label{eq:rawvsactivated}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal{T}_0$ is the seed. The left equality is why the conflation is
tempting --- the raw span really does exhaust $\Ften$ --- and the strict
inclusion on the right is the entire content of theorem~\ref{thm:reach}. The raw
span is retained in the test suite as a negative fixture so the error cannot
recur silently.

\subsection{The exact rational computation}
The closure is a fixed-point computation, and running it modulo $p$ would leave
the answer exposed to exceptional primes in precisely the place where no
spanning-set argument is available. We therefore ran it over $\Q$.

Of the closure's targets, $\czIntegerRows$ were already integral. The remaining
$\czLiftedRows$ were lifted by CRT across $\czFitPrimes$ fitting primes followed
by rational reconstruction, and the lift was validated at the held-out prime
$\czHoldoutPrime$, with no mismatches. The closure was then iterated in exact
$\mathbb{Q}$ arithmetic and reached its fixed point after $\czSweeps$ sweeps.

It is worth showing why this was necessary rather than merely careful, because
the cost of exact arithmetic is real and a reader is entitled to ask whether one
modular solve would have done. Figure~\ref{fig:heights} plots the size of the
largest coefficient the closure actually produces at each degree, taken from its
own exact output. Through degree eight the coordinates are small integers and
nothing is at risk. At degree ten one basis vector of the reachable space
carries a numerator of twenty-nine bits over a five-digit denominator --- an
order of magnitude beyond what a single prime near $2^{15}$ can represent. Read
modulo one such prime that coefficient is indistinguishable from a small
residue, and the fixed point would have been reported at the wrong dimension
with nothing in the output to indicate it. The lift is what makes the degree-ten
row recoverable at all.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.72\textwidth]{figures/fig05_rational_heights.pdf}
\caption{Size of the largest numerator and denominator appearing in a basis
vector of the flow-reachable space, by degree, in bits. The dashed line is the
representable range of a single prime near $2^{15}$. Degree ten is the first
place the exact coefficients leave that range, which is why that row is lifted
by the Chinese remainder theorem and rational reconstruction rather than read
off one modular solve.}
\label{fig:heights}
\end{figure}

\begin{theorem}[Exact degree-ten reachability]
\label{thm:reach}
Over the rationals,
\begin{equation}
\dim_\Q \Ften = \dimAtenQ,
\qquad
\dim_\Q \Dten = \dimDtenQ,
\qquad
\dim_\Q \Qten \;\czQtenRelation\; \dimQtenQ .
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

The last equality deserves a word, because it is stronger than the modular
computation it replaced. Running the closure over $\Q$ removes the modular
admission test that made the earlier figure a lower bound. At the fixed point no
further generated direction raises the rank over $\Q$, so the reached span
\emph{is} $\Dten$ and its rank is an equality, not a bound. No separate
upper-bound argument is required. Table~\ref{tab:degree10} lists the
degree-ten invariants and the block each occupies.

\input{tables/tab07_degree10.tex}

The lower-bound side is certified by an explicit $\czMinorSize \times
\czMinorSize$ integer minor with non-zero determinant, computed by Bareiss
elimination and confirmed by an independent exact rational verifier. Three exact
annihilating covectors exhibit the quotient directly, and the quotient
representatives are indexed by the free columns not occupied by a pivot.

\input{tables/tab08_quotient.tex}

\subsection{Reading the result}
There are $\dimQtenQ$ independent degree-ten invariant directions that the stress
flow does not reach. The subspaces of $\Ften$ that this paper determines exactly stand in the
relations
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
\Dten \subsetneq \Ften,
\qquad
\dim_\Q \Ften/\Dten = \dimQtenQ,
\\[2pt]
\dim_\Q(\Bten \cap \Pten) = \dimBcapP,
\qquad
\dim_\Q(\Bten + \Pten) = \dimBplusP,
\end{gathered}
\label{eq:incidence}
\end{equation}
with $\dim_\Q \Bten = \dimBten$ and $\dim_\Q \Pten = \dimPten$; the last two
are established in section~\ref{sec:published}. Every dimension in
\eqref{eq:incidence} is exact over $\Q$, not modulo a prime.

\subsection{How many directions are needed, in any basis}
\begin{proposition}[Cardinality minimality]
\label{prop:cardinality}
If $S \subset \Ften$ is any set with $\Dten + \mathrm{span}(S) = \Ften$, then
$|S| \ge \dim \Qten$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Apply the quotient map $\pi: \Ften \to \Qten$. From
$\Dten + \mathrm{span}(S) = \Ften$ we get $\mathrm{span}(\pi(S)) = \Qten$, and a
span of $|S|$ vectors has dimension at most $|S|$.
\end{proof}
This is elementary linear algebra and we claim no novelty for it. We state it
because it converts a basis-dependent assertion into a basis-free one: no
closing set of any kind, in any basis, has fewer than $\dimQtenQ$ elements. What
it does \emph{not} give is removal minimality of the particular set we exhibit,
which we have checked only in the fixed graph basis and under the permutation
subgroup, and which remains open in general (section~\ref{sec:limitations}).

% ================================================================ 10
\section{The free stress-tensor trace and activation}
\label{sec:gten}

The leading-degree bookkeeping of the closure rests on one physical input: the
degree at which $\operatorname{Tr}(\tau)$ first contributes. If it began at degree
two rather than four, every generated target would land in the wrong graded piece
and theorem~\ref{thm:reach} would fall with it. This section derives the input.

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing of the quadratic trace]
\label{thm:gten}
For a self-dual five-form in ten dimensions, the free stress tensor has vanishing
trace, so $\operatorname{Tr}(\tau)$ first contributes at field degree four.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write the free stress tensor of a $p$-form field strength in $d$ dimensions in
its general improved form,
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
T_{\mu\nu}
 \;=\; \frac{1}{(p-1)!}\,F_{\mu\alpha_2\dots\alpha_p}\,
        F_\nu{}^{\alpha_2\dots\alpha_p}
 \;-\; c\,\eta_{\mu\nu}\,\langle F,F\rangle,
\\[2pt]
\langle F,G\rangle \;=\; F_{\mu_1\dots\mu_p}G^{\mu_1\dots\mu_p},
\end{gathered}
\label{eq:stresstensor}
\end{equation}
with $c$ an improvement coefficient left free. Contracting with $\eta^{\mu\nu}$,
the first term returns $\langle F,F\rangle$ up to the normalisation carried by
the factorial and the second returns $-\,c\,d\,\langle F,F\rangle$, so
\begin{equation}
T^{\mu}{}_{\mu} \;=\; (1 - c\,d)\,\langle F,F\rangle .
\label{eq:tracescalar}
\end{equation}
Whatever $c$ may be, the trace is a multiple of the single scalar
$\langle F,F\rangle$; no other quadratic Lorentz invariant exists, since the only
way to contract two copies of a $p$-form into a scalar is the full contraction.
The conclusion below is therefore independent of the improvement term and of the
overall normalisation.

It remains to show that this one scalar vanishes. Specialise to $p = 5$, $d = 10$,
so that $F$ is a middle-degree form of \emph{odd} degree in an even-dimensional
space, and consider the top form $F\wedge F$. Interchanging two factors of a
$q$-form costs $(-1)^{q^2} = (-1)^{q}$, which for $q = 5$ is $-1$; hence
\begin{equation}
F\wedge F \;=\; -\,F\wedge F
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
F\wedge F \;\equiv\; 0
\label{eq:wedgevanishes}
\end{equation}
identically, for every five-form whatsoever. Since
$\langle F,\star F\rangle\,\mathrm{vol} \propto F\wedge F$, the pairing
$\langle F,\star F\rangle$ vanishes as well. On either eigenspace of the Hodge
star we have $\star F = \pm F$, and therefore
\begin{equation}
\langle F,F\rangle
 \;=\; \pm\,\langle F,\star F\rangle
 \;=\; 0 .
\label{eq:normvanishes}
\end{equation}
Substituting \eqref{eq:normvanishes} into \eqref{eq:tracescalar} gives
$T^{\mu}{}_{\mu} = 0$ for every $c$.
\end{proof}

Two features of this argument are worth isolating, because both are places where
a plausible-looking variant of the calculation gives a different answer.

The vanishing in \eqref{eq:wedgevanishes} is a statement about form parity alone
and holds for \emph{any} five-form, self-dual or not; self-duality enters only at
\eqref{eq:normvanishes}, to convert $\langle F,\star F\rangle$ into
$\langle F,F\rangle$. The two steps are independent, and a test suite that
checked only self-dual samples would confirm the conclusion without ever
exercising the mechanism behind it. Ours checks both eigenspaces --- the argument
predicts vanishing on each --- and, as a control, checks that
$\langle F,F\rangle \neq 0$ on an \emph{unprojected} five-form. Without that
control the first three checks would be satisfied vacuously by a quantity that
vanished for trivial reasons.

The sign $\star^2 = +\starSquared$ used in \eqref{eq:normvanishes} is
signature-dependent. In Euclidean signature $\star^2 = -1$ on middle-degree forms
in ten dimensions, the eigenvalues are $\pm i$, and there is no real eigenspace
decomposition to speak of. This is not a hypothetical: an earlier version of the
control called a projector routine with an argument believed to select the
anti-self-dual space when it in fact selected Euclidean signature, and the
resulting non-vanishing was briefly read as signal. The value of $\star^2$ is now
asserted by test wherever the decomposition is used rather than presumed.

The argument is short, and its shortness is the point: it uses no property of the
particular theory beyond self-duality and the parity of the form degree, so it
survives any reformulation of the free dynamics.

\begin{remark}[Free versus deformed trace]
Theorem~\ref{thm:gten} is about the \emph{free} stress tensor, while the flow
\eqref{eq:flow} involves the deformed $\tau$. This is the right object for the
purpose. The grading argument needs only the field degree at which
$\operatorname{Tr}(\tau)$ \emph{begins}, and the leading term of the deformed
trace is the free trace: the deformation contributes corrections of strictly
higher degree. We make no claim that the deformed trace vanishes --- in general
it does not, which is precisely what makes the flow non-trivial.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Which stress tensor, and why this is a review item]
The theorem establishes tracelessness for a stress tensor of the standard
$p$-form shape with an arbitrary improvement term. Whether the object appearing
in the flow of \cite{Hutomo:2025chiral} is of that shape, in the formulation the
authors intend, is a question about their conventions rather than about our
computation, and we have not been able to settle it from the published text
alone. Because every degree-ten result depends on it, we flag it explicitly as
review item \textbf{G-10} rather than assuming the favourable reading. If the
intended object is of a different shape, the improvement-independence above means
the conclusion is likely to survive, but ``likely'' is not the standard the rest
of this paper is held to.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Verification, with a control.}
The computational half is checked by code that imports no flow machinery,
re-deriving the statement from the five-form and the Hodge star alone. The
vanishing is confirmed on both eigenspaces at four primes. Crucially the suite
also contains a \emph{control}: $\langle F,F\rangle$ must \emph{not} vanish on an
unprojected five-form. Without that control the vanishing tests would prove
nothing, since a function that vanished identically would pass them all.

\paragraph{The counterfactual.}
To show the derivation is load-bearing rather than decorative we forced the
opposite assumption --- $\operatorname{Tr}(\tau)$ beginning at degree two --- and
re-ran the closure. The result is $\Qten = \gTenCounterfactualQten$, against
$\gTenDerivedQten$ as derived, with the degree-ten reachable dimension rising to
$\dimAten$ and swallowing the whole atlas. The counterfactual reproduces exactly
the wrong answer this project obtained at an earlier stage, and it is retained as
a regression fixture.

\input{tables/tab11_tests.tex}

\section{The published basis and the product sector}
\label{sec:published}

Let $\Bten$ denote the span of the degree-ten structures given in
\cite{Cederwall:2025invariants}, and $\Pten$ the product subspace. Both are
spanned by explicit elements, so their rational dimensions follow from modular
ranks with no prime excluded:
$\dim_\Q \Bten = \dimBten$ and $\dim_\Q \Pten = \dimPten$.

The interesting quantity is the intersection. To settle it over $\Q$ we lifted
all $\dimBten$ published coordinate vectors by CRT across $\bpFitPrimes$ fitting
primes and rational reconstruction, validated at the held-out prime
$\bpHoldoutPrime$ with no mismatches, and computed the intersection exactly.

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:bp}
$\dim_\Q(\Bten \cap \Pten) \;\bpCapRelation\; \dimBcapP$, and
$\dim_\Q(\Bten + \Pten) = \dimBplusP$.
\end{theorem}

The one-dimensional intersection can be written out. With $I^{(k)}$ denoting the
published structures in the numbering of \cite{Cederwall:2025invariants} and
$I^{(4)}_1 I^{(6)}_1$ the product of the degree-four and degree-six invariants,
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
-55\,I^{(1)} - 252\,I^{(2)}& + 4200\,I^{(5)} + 5040\,I^{(6)} \\
 &=\; -1040\,I^{(4)}_1 I^{(6)}_1 .
\end{split}
\label{eq:bpidentity}
\end{equation}
This identity was verified at the fresh prime $\bpFreshPrime$ on
$\bpFreshSamples$ independently drawn samples, none of which were used in the
reconstruction.

Because \eqref{eq:bpidentity} carries specific integer coefficients, it is not
invariant under rescaling the objects entering it, unlike every rank and
dimension elsewhere in this paper. The coefficients are stated relative to the
normalisation of the published structures in \cite{Cederwall:2025invariants} and
of the degree-four and degree-six invariants fixed in
appendix~\ref{app:blocks}. Under a rescaling $I^{(k)} \to c_k I^{(k)}$ the
coefficients transform by the inverse factors; what is normalisation-independent
is the statement that the intersection is one-dimensional and that its generator
is supported on the four published structures listed. The published basis is
given in table~\ref{tab:b10} and the product sector in
table~\ref{tab:products}.

\input{tables/tab09_b10.tex}
\input{tables/tab04_spans.tex}

\paragraph{Consequences.}
The published span contains exactly one product direction, so its non-product
content is $\publishedPrimitiveContent$-dimensional. In particular $\Bten$ is not
a complement to the products. This is a structural fact about the published
choice of structures, not a criticism of it: nothing in
\cite{Cederwall:2025invariants} claims otherwise, and the structures there are
presented as explicit expressions rather than as a basis with specified relations.

\begin{remark}[A check that failed first]
The verification of \eqref{eq:bpidentity} initially failed at a fresh prime, on
all six samples. The cause was in the check, not the identity: the two sides were
being reduced by their greatest common divisors separately, which destroys the
relative scale that the identity is precisely about. Recomputing on a single
common scale, it holds. We record this because a check that fails and is then
quietly adjusted until it passes is worth nothing, and the only defence against
that is to say what was adjusted and why.
\end{remark}

\input{tables/tab03_products.tex}

\section{Reproducibility and proof architecture}
\label{sec:repro}

The results above are computational, and a computational result that cannot be
re-run is an assertion. The architecture supporting them has the following
components.

\paragraph{Test suites.} $\nTraceTests$ tests on the tensor side and
$\nBridgeTests$ on the bridge side, run from a clean clone.

\paragraph{Counterfactual and mutation tests.} Several tests deliberately break
an assumption and assert the consequence: the G-10 counterfactual
(section~\ref{sec:gten}), the orientation branch flip
(section~\ref{sec:orientation}), and the raw-target negative fixture
(section~\ref{sec:reach}). These matter more than the passing tests, because a
suite that only confirms what the code already does cannot detect a shared
assumption that is wrong.

\paragraph{Generated macros.} Every scientific number in this document is a macro
expanded from \texttt{generated/numbers.tex}, which is produced from result
artifacts. Typing a number into the prose is prevented by convention and checked
by the claim gates.

\paragraph{Claim gates.} A set of automated checks run against the compiled
source, each testing a specific wording or consistency requirement --- that no
unscoped completeness or canonicality claim appears, that a quantity certified as
a bound is never described as an equality, that documentation does not contradict
the artifacts. Each gate was negative-tested: deliberately violated, to confirm it
fails.

\paragraph{Immutable artifacts and deterministic aggregation.} Cells are written
once and aggregated read-only, with the aggregation independent of order.

\paragraph{Deterministic figures and byte-reproducible archives.} Figures are
generated from artifacts with timestamps suppressed, so repeated runs produce
byte-identical output. The tests run along that route are summarised in table~\ref{tab:tests}, and the
route itself is short enough to state in a sentence: from a clean clone, the
suites run, the certificate scripts regenerate their artifacts, the figures and
tables are rebuilt from those artifacts, the macros are extracted, the manuscript
compiles, and every gate must pass or the build fails.

Table~\ref{tab:certificates} lists every certificate the draft rests on, with
the script that produced it, and table~\ref{tab:environment} records the
environment the certified runs were made in.

\input{tables/tab10_certificates.tex}
\input{tables/tab12_environment.tex}

\section{Physical interpretation}
\label{sec:physics}

We are deliberately cautious here, and we separate what has been established from
what it might mean.

What has been established is a statement about a construction: the stress-tensor
flow, as formulated in \cite{Hutomo:2025chiral} and in the conventions fixed in
appendix~\ref{app:conventions}, does not reach $\dimQtenQ$ independent directions
of the degree-ten invariant space. That is a fact about the flow, not about
nature.

It is nonetheless a suggestive fact, because the analogous question in six
dimensions appears to have a different answer. There the chiral two-form theories
and their $T\bar T$-like flows are reported to exhibit a
universality~\cite{Ferko:2024chiral,Brizio:2026ttbar}. We take that
characterisation from those works; we have not verified their results and the
comparison is theirs, not ours. Read that way, the ten-dimensional degree-ten
sector may be the first place in this programme where the flow provably fails to
be exhaustive --- but establishing that it is the first would require a survey we
have not done. Whether the missed directions correspond to genuinely inaccessible
deformations, or merely to deformations this particular flow does not generate,
is not settled by anything here.

The trace structure of section~\ref{sec:gten} is a conformal statement in the
free theory and it is standard; we use it as an input to the grading, not as a
result.

\paragraph{Type IIB, as motivation only.}
This paragraph is context for why the problem is worth attention; it establishes
nothing and no later statement depends on it. The self-dual five-form is the
Ramond--Ramond field strength of Type IIB supergravity, whose covariant field
equations were given by Schwarz~\cite{Schwarz:1983qr} and for which manifestly
Lorentz-invariant actions were later constructed by Dall'Agata, Lechner and
Tonin~\cite{DallAgata:1998ahf} using precisely the chiral-boson machinery
referred to above. Higher-derivative corrections involving the five-form have
been studied directly~\cite{Paulos:2008tn}, within the broader eight-derivative
programme~\cite{Green:1997as,Liu:2022bfg}, and non-perturbatively through
D-instanton contributions to the $R^4$ sector~\cite{Green:1997tv}. It is natural to ask whether the
degree-ten invariants classified here constrain those corrections. We do not
answer that question and we make no Type IIB claim. The obstacles are concrete:
the corrections live in a supersymmetric theory with additional fields, the
relevant invariants are not obviously the Lorentz invariants of a free five-form
in isolation, and the action formulation carries the well-known
difficulties~\cite{Marcus:1982yu,Sen:2019qit}. We record Type IIB as context and
as motivation, and nothing in this paper should be read as a prediction about it.

\paragraph{What is explicitly not claimed.}
No Type IIB effective-action prediction. No statement about causal propagation or
hyperbolicity of any deformed theory. No supersymmetry statement. No all-order
theorem about the flow.

% ================================================================ 14
\section{Limitations and open problems}
\label{sec:limitations}

\begin{enumerate}\itemsep3pt

\item \textbf{Generator extension.} We compute what the flow reaches from the
generators it is given. Whether an enlarged generator set reaches more of
$\Ften$ is not addressed.

\item \textbf{Removal minimality.} Proposition~\ref{prop:cardinality} gives
cardinality minimality in any basis. Removal minimality of the particular closing
set we exhibit --- that no element of it can be dropped --- has been checked only
in the fixed graph basis and under the permutation subgroup. Minimality under
arbitrary $GL$ change of basis would require regenerating the certificates in the
new basis and has not been attempted.

\item \textbf{No canonicality.} We exhibit bases; we do not claim any of them is
canonical or unique, and no such claim should be read into the word ``basis''.

\item \textbf{Enumeration exhaustiveness is corroborated, not proved.} Every
dimension in this paper is exact for the span of the candidate family we
enumerate. Identifying that span with the space of \emph{all} degree-ten
Lorentz invariants requires the enumeration to be exhaustive, and we do not
prove that it is. What we have is two independently implemented constructions,
contraction graphs and chiral bispinors, whose spans agree at degrees four, six,
eight and ten; a missing invariant would have to have been missed twice, in two
different languages. That is corroboration and it is not a theorem. A proof
would need a Hilbert-series or character-theoretic count of the degree-ten
invariants of the $\dimSelfDualModule$-dimensional module, which we have not
carried out and which is the single most valuable check anyone could add to
this work.

\item \textbf{Degree twelve.} Degree twelve supplies partial certified input to
the generic rank calculation and is excluded from this paper's tensor--spinor
equivalence and degree-ten classification claims. We do not claim a complete
degree-twelve equivalence.

\item \textbf{No invariant-ring presentation.} We give dimensions and bases of
graded pieces, not generators and relations for the full invariant ring, and no
Hilbert series is claimed as a result here.

\item \textbf{No all-order flow theorem.} Everything about reachability is stated
at degree ten. No induction to all orders is offered.

\item \textbf{Rank-matrix independence.} Two of the $\matrixCells$ cells were
independently recomputed in this repository. The other thirteen carry internal
consistency and a shared ordering hash, which is weaker.

\item \textbf{A source ambiguity, avoided rather than resolved.} Two of the
published degree-ten expressions are ambiguous as printed, because bracket colour
--- which fixes the order of operations --- does not survive text extraction. We
implemented both readings and report the consequences of each, and the compact
$\Qten$ basis is chosen to avoid the ambiguous candidates entirely, so no result
here depends on the resolution. The ambiguity is avoided, not resolved;
confirming the source's intent requires its authors.

\item \textbf{Physical interpretation.} As set out in
section~\ref{sec:physics}, the reachability result is a statement about a
construction. Its physical significance is open.

\item \textbf{``Basis'' is used loosely.} We exhibit spanning sets of the stated
dimension and call them bases. Since removal minimality is open in general
(item 2), a reader should read ``basis'' throughout as ``spanning set of
cardinality equal to the dimension'', which is what is certified.

\item \textbf{No Hilbert-series cross-check.} The natural independent check on
graded dimensions would be a Hilbert series for the invariant ring. We did not
compute one. Its absence is a missing corroboration rather than a defect, but a
reader entitled to expect it should know it is not here.

\item \textbf{Held-out primes.} The $\Dten$ lift was validated at one held-out
prime; the $\Bten$ lift at one held-out prime and again on fresh samples at a
further prime. A single held-out prime leaves a probability of order $1/p$ per
row of a silent false pass. That is small, and it is not zero.

\item \textbf{Independence of the two determinant routines.} The Bareiss and
exact-rational routines are separate implementations but share this project's
modular-arithmetic layer. A defect confined to that layer would not be caught by
their agreement.

\item \textbf{The macro-generation link.} Every number in this paper is
generated from an artifact by one script. A defect in that script would
propagate to the prose and to the claim gates alike, since both read its output.
The mitigation is that the gates compare macros against \emph{independently
parsed} artifact fields rather than against each other, but the link is a single
point of failure and we name it as one.

\item \textbf{Optional-dependency code path.} The certified runs used the
built-in contraction ordering because \texttt{opt\_einsum} was not installed. We
expect the accelerated path to give identical values, since contraction order
affects speed and not arithmetic, but we did not run the full certification both
ways, so this is an expectation rather than a verified claim.

\end{enumerate}

Table~\ref{tab:claimstrength} classifies every claim in the paper by the
strength of the evidence behind it, from theorem to expectation.

\input{tables/tab13_claim_strength.tex}

% ================================================================ 15
\section{Conclusions}
\label{sec:conclusions}

We have determined the degree-ten Lorentz-invariant structure of a self-dual
five-form in ten dimensions, exactly and with certificates.

The full degree-ten invariant space has dimension $\dimAtenQ$ over $\Q$. The
subspace reachable by the stress-tensor flow has dimension $\dimDtenQ$, and the
quotient therefore has dimension $\dimQtenQ$: three independent directions the
flow does not reach. Both dimensions are established over the rationals, not
merely modulo a prime, by lifting the closure's targets and running it to its
fixed point in exact rational arithmetic. The span of the published degree-ten
structures meets the product sector in exactly one dimension, and that
intersection is written out as an explicit integer identity,
equation~\eqref{eq:bpidentity}.

Supporting these are an exact tensor--spinor bridge of certified rank
$\bridgeForwardRank$ with an exact left inverse, a degree-resolved verification
that the two formulations span the same invariants at degrees four, six, eight
and ten, and an exact lower bound of $\charZeroLowerBound$ on the generic
functional rank of the candidate family, certified by an explicit
$\minorSize\times\minorSize$ minor. The matching upper bound is analytic and is
due to earlier work.

Along the way two defects in our own earlier treatment were found and corrected:
the conflation of the raw target span with the flow-reachable subspace, which had
produced a quotient dimension of zero, and an unpinned square-root branch in the
frame construction, which had left the self-dual and anti-self-dual channels to
be selected by accident. Both are now covered by tests that fail if the defect
returns.

The open questions we regard as most interesting are whether the three missed
directions have a physical meaning, and whether an enlarged generator set would
reach them.
